note: SMAD2 truncating variants are documented to cause complex CHD, heterotaxy, developmental delay, and syndromic features in addition to vascular aneurysms.

evidence.text: Whole exome sequencing identified truncating, splice, and deleterious missense variants in SMAD2 in probands presenting with complex CHD, developmental delay, dysmorphic features, and fetal heterotaxy, demonstrating an early-onset congenital/syndromic phenotype alongside late-onset vascular disease.

source.title: Variable cardiovascular phenotypes associated with SMAD2 pathogenic variants
source.quote: Our data suggest two distinct phenotypes associated with pathogenic variants in SMAD2: complex CHD with or without laterality defects and other congenital anomalies, and a late-onset vascular phenotype characterized by arterial aneurysms with connective tissue abnormalities.

evidence.text: De novo protein-truncating, splicing, and deleterious missense variants in SMAD2 were identified across cohorts of patients presenting with heterotaxy and congenital heart disease.

source.title: Genetics of Congenital Heart Disease
source.quote: De novo protein-truncating, splicing, and deleterious missense variants in SMAD2 were identified in a cohort of CHD patients with a variety of defects
